citations.text: Dietvorst, B. J., Simmons, J. P., & Massey, C. (2015). Algorithm aversion: People erroneously avoid algorithms after seeing them err. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 144(1), 114-126.

en.general: Choosing a human's judgment over an algorithm's after seeing the algorithm make a mistake, even when relying on the algorithm would have worked better. Wording for students: trusting a program less after it errs once, more than we would trust a person who erred the same way.

examples: A forecasting task in which people stop following a computer forecaster after seeing it miss, although it was the better forecaster.
